sound: These audit fixes check out in the code: the LEI read in part, Companies House pages that fail, officer pagination, PSC/charges/insolvency, jurisdiction-aware state registers, the state coverage note, switches for the exposure sources, patents and trademarks honestly off, and the HIBP check against the company's own domain. The registers in registriesIntl.js are gated by country and grade a company on its name only when that name has two words. The infostealer lookup is off by default and reads counts only. All other leak and breach records are labelled 'claimed, unverified' and kept at company level. The temporary test file was deleted.

findings.title: Breach sources show a namesake as the company's breach when the company name is '<word> AI' or '<word> Labs'
findings.evidence: zz test: subject Harvey AI, HIBP entry 'Harvey' (harveys-furniture.example) came back as company, medium. gradeOrganisation for 'Mistral, Inc.' and 'Mistral' gave company. isOrdinaryWordCompany('Harvey AI') returns true, but distinctiveName never asks it.
findings.scenario: Company 'Harvey AI', 'Scale AI' or 'Mistral AI'. isCompanyName treats the bare brand ('Harvey', 'Mistral, Inc.') as an exact match. distinctiveName then passes because key.full has two words, even though 'ai' is padding. The result: 'Harvey data breach, 1 May 2019: 120,000 accounts' is graded company, severity medium. The same happens in breachRegistersMore.distinctive, leakSitesMore.distinctiveName and the RansomLook catalogue.
findings.fix: Judge distinctiveness on key.core, not key.full: distinctive = specific && (core.length >= 2 || !isOrdinaryWordCompany(core.join(' '))). Make the same change in exposure.js, breachRegistersMore.js and leakSitesMore.js. A bare-brand match on an ordinary core is then possible, kept off the timeline and fixed. Add tests for 'Harvey AI' against 'Harvey' and for 'Mistral AI' against 'Mistral, Inc.'.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. In breachRegistersMore, 'Harvey' and 'Scale' were graded company, medium, for Harvey AI and Scale AI. isCompanyName accepts the bare core. distinctive/distinctiveName read key.full, which has 2 words because of 'ai'. The same code is in exposure.js:295 and leakSitesMore.js:148.
findings.betterFix: Judge distinctiveness on the form that matched, not always on core. If the entry matched only key.core (the bare brand), require core.length>=2 or !isOrdinaryWordCompany(core). An exact full match ('Harvey AI, Inc.') must stay company; the proposed core-only rule would demote it and thin the profile. Have isCompanyName return 'core' for the bare-brand branch so callers can tell the two apart.

findings.title: Patents: a name-only family with a look-alike assignee is still graded confirmed (audit finding not fixed)
findings.evidence: zz test with FOUNDER_GOOGLE_PATENTS=on: John Smith / Flow, name search returned US1A with assignee 'Flow Hair Salon Inc'. Result: US1A 'confirmed', reason 'names Flow'. The summary was also confirmed and counted 3 families. Flowserve was correctly held at possible.
findings.scenario: Only a family returned by the assignee=Flow search is held. A family from the name search alone whose assignee resembles the company ('Flow Hair Salon Inc') gets heldGrade null, because anchors.test does not match it. It then goes to the general grader with the assignee in matchText, and the grader finds 'Flow' and sets confirmed. The patent is off by default, so this happens only when the owner turns it on.
findings.fix: In heldGrade, before returning null, also hold at possible with matchFixed when any assignee passes resemblesCompany(a, companyShort) but fails assigneeCompany. More generally, take name-only families out of the grader: strip assignees that are not assigneeCompany() from matchText (keep them in the quote and data). Leave the summary matchText to tied families only.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced through patentsConnector.run with FOUNDER_GOOGLE_PATENTS=on. The name search alone returned assignee 'Flow Hair Salon Inc'. US1A came back confirmed, 'names Flow'. heldGrade returns null because anchors.test rejects the look-alike. Called directly, makeFinding grades it possible, so something on the connector path, probably how the bolded assignee text is parsed, is what ties it.
findings.betterFix: In heldGrade, before returning null, hold the family at possible with matchFixed when any assignee passes resemblesCompany(a, companyShort) but fails assigneeCompany. Also find out why the parsed assignee or matchText ties it (log family.assignees for 'Flow Hair Salon Inc'). Add a name-search-only regression test next to the existing assignee-search one.

findings.title: RansomFeed ties an exact-name listing to the company although it names a different website from the company's own
findings.evidence: zz test: Nikola with own domain nikolamotor.com. RansomFeed row victim 'Nikola', website nikola-hotel.rs, returned 'Nikola listed by akira on a ransomware leak site', match company, severity medium.
findings.scenario: The company's own site is known. A RansomFeed post names the same distinctive name but gives another website. Line 181 drops only non-exact grades on another site, so the exact name match on a stranger's site is kept and graded company. The comment above it says the opposite ('a merge.cd is not merge.dev'), and HIBP (exposure.js:636) skips such entries.
findings.fix: When own.length and the row gives a site that is not in own, return null, or at most grade possible with matchFixed and the note 'the listing gives the website X, not the company's'. Keep the HIBP behaviour as the rule, and add a test with a distinctive name on a foreign website.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. A row with victim 'Nikola' and website nikola-hotel.rs was graded company, medium, with the own domain nikola.com, because line 181 drops only non-exact grades. With nikolamotor.com it also failed, for a different reason: ownDomainsOf keeps only domains whose label is exactly the name, so own was empty.
findings.betterFix: In matchListing, when the row gives a website and the company has any known domain (use the subject's domain anchors and domain aliases for this company, not only domains named exactly like it), grade the listing possible with matchFixed and a note naming the other website, or drop it as HIBP does. Fix ownDomainsOf the same way so nikolamotor.com counts as the company's own.

findings.title: Domain history compares every domain with the given company's founding year, so an earlier company's domain is labelled as bought from an earlier holder
findings.evidence: zz test: subject.foundedYear=2019 (Ramp), domain task paribus.co with no params, RDAP registration 2013. Title: 'registered 6 years before the stated 2019 founding: registered by an earlier holder and acquired later'. earlierHolder and excludeFromTimeline were both true.
findings.scenario: deepCheck.companyDomainYear passes foundedYear only for the given company's own domain. But foundingYearFor falls back to ctx.subject.foundedYear for any domain, which deepCheck sets on the subject. The domain of the founder's earlier start-up (or a later one) is then flagged as bought from an earlier holder or 'registered N years after the stated founding' (low severity). It is also dropped from the timeline and from WHAT CHECKS OUT.
findings.fix: Remove the ctx.subject.foundedYear fallback. Use only task.params.foundedYear (already gated by companyDomainYear) or a tied record that names this exact domain. Add a test with subject.foundedYear set and a domain of another company.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. foundingYearFor('paribus.co') with params null returned {year:2019, from:'given'} through the ctx.subject.foundedYear fallback, which deepCheck sets at lines 516 and 1277. That undoes the companyDomainYear gate, so an earlier company's domain gets the earlier-holder flag and is taken off the timeline.
findings.betterFix: Remove the ctx.subject.foundedYear fallback and rely on task.params.foundedYear or a tied record for this exact domain. report.js step 5 (earlierHolder, about line 741) applies companyFoundedYear to every domain-history finding and has the same flaw: limit it to the company's own domains.

findings.title: US state registers take the home state from a tied record of any of the person's companies
findings.evidence: zz test: ctx.findings held an LEI 'company' record for another company with jurisdiction US-NV. Connecticut 'THERANOS, INC.' (formed in Delaware) was graded possible, 'another business'. Without that record it was graded company.
findings.scenario: homeJurisdiction(ctx) never looks at task.value. The first LEI record graded company, or the first SEC record with a state of incorporation (any issuer when the issuer is blank, or any known company), sets the 'home' state for every company task. With two companies in different states, the second company's true foreign registrations become 'another business', and a domestic namesake in the first company's state could be tied.
findings.fix: Pass the task's company to homeJurisdiction. Accept an LEI record only when knownCompanyFor(subject, its legal name) resolves to the same company as knownCompanyFor(subject, task.value). Require the SEC issuer to resolve to that company too, and drop the '!issuer' shortcut.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed by reading, not run. homeJurisdiction(ctx) never sees the task. It returns the state of the first LEI record graded company (any company) or of the first SEC record with a state (the !issuer shortcut). A second company is then judged against the first company's home state.
findings.betterFix: Pass task.value. Accept an LEI or SEC record only when knownCompanyFor(subject, its legal name or issuer) resolves to the same company as the task, and drop the !issuer shortcut. With no matching record, return null; no home state means no 'another business' demotion.

findings.title: A learned legal name found anywhere inside a register entry ties the entry as the company
findings.evidence: zz test: Bolt with learned alias 'Bolt Financial, Inc.'. gradeOrganisation(target, 'Lightning Bolt Financial Advisors LLC') returned grade legal, company, medium.
findings.scenario: After legal forms are stripped, a legal name like 'Bolt Financial, Inc.' or 'Ramp Business Corporation' becomes 'bolt financial' or 'ramp business'. containsRun accepts it anywhere in the entry, so 'Lightning Bolt Financial Advisors LLC' or 'Ramp Business Consulting Group' are graded the company's breach. exposure.js gradeMatch/nameGradeOf and leakSitesMore.legalNameIn use the same containsRun rule.
findings.fix: Treat a learned legal name like the given name: grade it with matchOrgName or isCompanyName (exact, or followed only by legal forms or padding) on each segment, not a substring run. Make 'company' depend on an exact match of the legal name. Anything looser is possible.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. With the alias 'Bolt Financial, Inc.', gradeOrganisation for 'Lightning Bolt Financial Advisors LLC' returned legal, company, medium. The same containsRun rule is in exposure.js (gradeMatch byLegalName, nameGradeOf, legalNameIn) and leakSitesMore.legalNameIn.
findings.betterFix: Tie on a learned legal name only when a segment is that name exactly, allowing trailing legal forms or padding (isCompanyName with the legal-name key). Grade a substring run as possible with a caution. Fix it in all three files with a shared helper.
